title: Poultry industry structure affects resilience to avian flu

analysis.time: The article was published on August 25, 2026. The study refers to the 2025-2026 HPAI season, which started on October 1, 2025. The HPAI outbreaks in Europe were reported as of August 19, 2026, and the last poultry case in the U.K. was recorded since May 1, 2026.

analysis.event: A study by the Royal Veterinary College and the University of Cambridge found that factors such as planning, infrastructure, and financial risk management significantly affect the resilience of the poultry industry to HPAI outbreaks. The study also notes that the H5N1 HPAI virus has been confirmed in outbreaks across Europe, with Poland having the highest number of cases.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In the 2025-2026 HPAI season, there were 100 confirmed outbreaks in the U.K., all involving the H5N1 virus. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study highlights the importance of planning, infrastructure, and insurance in managing HPAI outbreaks. Wild birds in Europe have experienced 2,672 outbreaks so far in 2026, with the H5N1 serotype detected in over 2,630 of these. The study emphasizes that biosecurity alone is insufficient, and industry-wide structural factors are equally important in protecting against avian flu.
